IncidentBot: Pager triggered: [ALERT] kvcache.eviction_ratio >= 0.10 on prod (auto-pager)
Priya M.: I'm on it — Quinn are you on-call?
Quinn (on-call): yep I'm here. looking at the dashboards now.
Tom R.: eviction_ratio spike started ~2125554200, correlates with per-route key-cardinality increase on route: /v1/embeddings/batch. hit_rate dropped from 93% -> 70% for affected shards.
Diego: seeing small uptick in 502s on edge for a handful of customers during the spike. SupportBot: auto-ticket #SUP-4890 created.
Helena: any deploys or cron jobs around that time?
Priya M.: CI deploys show a canary config push around 2125554100 to embeddings-preproc service. pinging infra if that correlates.
Quinn (on-call): mitigation ideas: (A) temporarily upsert `CACHE_CAPACITY` for embeddings namespace (B) throttle the large client job if identified (C) change alerting to reduce duplicate pages. going to try A first.
Tom R.: quick command to bump capacity on the cache-pool leader: `redis-cli -h kvcache-leader PSETEX cache:config:capacity 120000000` — doing now.
IncidentBot: config change applied by Tom R. (change id cfg-332)
Diego: within 90s eviction_ratio fell to ~0.065, hit_rate rising back to ~86% on most shards. some shards still at 75%.
Priya M.: muting noisy alarm `kvcache:eviction_ratio-prod` for 25m while we observe — note: log the mute with reason.
Tom R.: creating a new composite Datadog monitor to only page if evictions AND sustained latency increase:
```
alert when: avg(last_5m):avg:kvcache.eviction_ratio{env:prod} > 0.09
AND avg(last_5m):percentile(requests.latency_ms,95){env:prod} > 500
for: 5m
notify: #eng-oncall, runbook: https://dash.redwood/runbooks/kvcache-evictions
```
Helena: +1 on composite. also let's add a per-customer spike detection so we can mute for noisy tenants rather than global.
Diego: Support found 2 enterprise customers who saw repeated tail-latency ~800ms for ~3-6m. No data corruption. tickets: SUP-4890, SUP-4891. notified AE owners.
Quinn (on-call): handing over watch to Priya — I'm off in 30m. Priya ack?
Priya M.: ack. I'll keep monitoring attacker tenants and shard heatmap.
Diego: follow-up: we should add a dashboard that surfaces prefix-cardinality growth for top-50 prefixes and a churn metric (new_keys/min). I'll open an infra issue.
Priya M.: creating post-incident checklist: 1) Add per-shard eviction + hit_rate panels (done, temp) 2) Push composite monitor (Tom) 3) Add tenant-level throttles + alerting (Diego) 4) Document emergency knobs for on-call (Helena) 5) Prototype prefix-normalization for embeddings (product/ML)
Tom R.: PR link for monitor: https://git.redwood/monitors/2345 (draft)
Helena: one more: consider implementing an automated squelch that detects deploy windows and suppresses eviction alerts for short rolling updates — but still surface if latency is high.
Quinn (on-call): before I go — small canary test would be great. Diego, can you make a tiny load generator that creates high-cardinality keys for a minute so we can see behavior under controlled churn?
Diego: will do. scheduling a canary job `kvcache-cardinality-canary` in staging first.
SupportBot: Support summary: 2 customers impacted, transient high tail latency, no errors, tickets created.
IncidentBot: Incident RESOLVED by Priya M. — metrics stabilized and no further pages in the 30m observation window. Postmortem required.
Priya M.: I'll draft the postmortem and include graphs and the list of action items. assigning tasks: Tom -> composite monitor + runbook, Diego -> tenant throttles + canary job, Helena -> on-call emergency knobs doc, Quinn -> verify mute automation feasibility.
Tom R.: noted. will request review.
Helena: will also add a cloudwatch alert to detect sudden cardinality jumps (heuristic: new_keys_per_min > 100k)
Priya M.: thanks everyone. tagging infra/monitoring for follow-ups. closing thread :thumbsup:
